Create a Smooth Vector Plot Layer

Source: R/geom_vector_smooth.R
geom_vector_smooth.Rd

Usage

geom_vector_smooth(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "vector_smooth",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  n = c(11, 11),
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  method = "gam",
  se = TRUE,
  se.circle = FALSE,
  pi_type = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  formula = cbind(fx, fy) ~ x * y,
  eval_points = NULL,
  arrow = grid::arrow(angle = 20, length = unit(0.015, "npc"), type = "closed")
)

stat_vector_smooth(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  geom = "vector_smooth",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE,
  n = c(11, 11),
  xlim = NULL,
  ylim = NULL,
  method = "gam",
  se = TRUE,
  se.circle = FALSE,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  pi_type = NULL,
  formula = cbind(fx, fy) ~ x * y,
  eval_points = NULL,
  arrow = grid::arrow(angle = 20, length = unit(0.015, "npc"), type = "closed")
)

Arguments

mapping

A set of aesthetic mappings created by ggplot2::aes(). Required: Must include x and y; vector displacements are defined by fx and fy.

data

A data frame containing the raw vector data.

stat

The statistical transformation. geom_vector_smooth() always uses StatVectorSmooth, which fits the model; another value is ignored with a warning.

position

Position adjustment, either as a string or the result of a position adjustment function.

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::layer() and the underlying geometry/stat.

n

An integer vector specifying the number of grid points along each axis for smoothing.

xlim, ylim

Numeric vectors of length 2 giving the range of the grid on which the smoothed field is evaluated when eval_points is NULL. They default to the range of the data.

method

Character. Specifies the smoothing method. Supported options are "gam" (default), "lm", and "kriging". The "gam" method fits fx and fy together, each with the smooth s(x, y), in mgcv's multivariate normal family (mgcv::mvn()), which also estimates the correlation of their residuals; the "lm" method fits the multivariate linear model given by formula, and "kriging" uses a cokriging approach via the gstat package. Each smooth uses up to 30 basis functions, and at most half as many as there are distinct locations; at least 5 locations are needed. With fewer than 10 locations, or data without noise, fx and fy are fitted separately and their residuals are taken to be uncorrelated.

se

Logical. If TRUE, prediction intervals for the tip of each vector are computed and plotted. For every method they cover a new observation at that location, not only the fitted mean: their covariance is the covariance of the fitted vector plus the residual covariance, so ellipses tilt when fx and fy are correlated.

se.circle

Logical. Defaults to FALSE. If TRUE, circles are drawn around the origin of each vector. By default, the circle’s radius is computed as the magnitude of the predicted vector.

pi_type

Character. Determines the display style for prediction intervals. By default (NULL), ellipses are drawn at eval_points and wedges on a grid.

  • "ellipse": Ellipses are used to represent the covariance of the predictions.

  • "wedge": Angular wedges show the prediction interval for the direction of each vector: the central conf_level range of the angle of its tip, from the exact distribution of that angle when the tip is normally distributed with the predicted mean and covariance.

  • "length": A band along each vector shows the prediction interval for its length: the central conf_level range of the length of its tip, from the exact distribution of that length. On a grid, where the vectors are drawn at a common length, each band is scaled with its vector and cut off at twice the vector's drawn length. Ellipses are a joint region for the tip; wedges and length bands are each an interval for one coordinate, the direction or the length, and only one type is drawn at a time. Ellipses need eval_points: if pi_type = "ellipse" is set and eval_points is NULL, wedges are drawn instead, with a warning.

conf_level

Numeric. Specifies the confidence level for the prediction intervals. Default is 0.95. If a vector is given, its first element is used.

formula

A formula specifying the multivariate linear model used for smoothing when method = "lm". The default is cbind(fx, fy) ~ x * y. It is ignored by the other methods, with a warning if it is supplied when method = "gam".

eval_points

A data frame of evaluation points. If provided, these specify the grid where the smoothing model is evaluated. If NULL, a grid is generated based on n.

arrow

A grid::arrow() specification for arrowheads on the smoothed vectors.

Value

A ggplot2 layer that can be added to a plot to create a smooth vector field visualization.

Details

geom_vector_smooth() creates a ggplot2 layer that visualizes a smooth vector field. It takes raw vector data and applies smoothing (by default a generalized additive model; a multivariate linear model or cokriging are also available via method) to estimate the underlying vector field. This functionality is analogous to geom_smooth() in ggplot2 but is tailored for vector data rather than scalar responses.

Aesthetics

geom_vector_smooth() supports the following aesthetics (required aesthetics are in bold):

  • x: The x-coordinate of the vector's starting point.

  • y: The y-coordinate of the vector's starting point.

  • fx: The horizontal component of the vector displacement.

  • fy: The vertical component of the vector displacement.

  • color: The color of the vector lines.

  • linewidth: The thickness of the vector lines.

  • linetype: The type of the vector lines (e.g., solid, dashed).

  • alpha: The transparency level of the vectors.

  • arrow: An aesthetic that can be used to modify arrowhead properties.

Details

Multivariate Linear Model: The "lm" method fits a multivariate linear model to predict vector displacements (fx and fy) based on the coordinates x and y, including interaction terms (x * y). This model smooths the raw vector data to provide an estimate of the underlying vector field.

Prediction Intervals: When se = TRUE, prediction intervals are computed for the smoothed vectors. Three types of intervals are supported:

  • Ellipse: Ellipses represent the joint uncertainty (covariance) in the predicted fx and fy.

  • Wedge: Wedges (angular sectors) show the range of likely directions of each vector; their radius is the predicted vector's length.

  • Length: Bands along each vector show the range of likely lengths. The type of interval displayed is controlled by pi_type, and the confidence level is set via conf_level.

Examples

# Function to generate vectors
generate_vectors <- function(v) {
  x <- v[1]
  y <- v[2]
  c(
    sin(x) + sin(y) + rnorm(1, 5, 1),
    sin(x) - sin(y) - rnorm(1, 5, 1)
  )
}

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Create sample points and compute vectors
sample_points <- data.frame(
  x = runif(30, 0, 10),
  y = runif(30, 0, 10)
)

result <- t(apply(sample_points, 1, generate_vectors))

sample_points$xend <- result[, 1]
sample_points$yend <- result[, 2]
sample_points$fx <- sample_points$xend - sample_points$x
sample_points$fy <- sample_points$yend - sample_points$y
sample_points$distance <- sqrt(sample_points$fx^2 + sample_points$fy^2)
sample_points$angle <- atan2(sample_points$fy, sample_points$fx)

# Define evaluation points
eval_points <- data.frame(
  x = c(0, 7.5),
  y = c(10, 5)
)

# Example 1:
ggplot(sample_points, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_vector(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy, color = NULL), center = FALSE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vector_smooth(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy), n = 5) +
  ggtitle("Smoothed Vector Field")


# Example 2: Ellipse with eval_points
ggplot(sample_points, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_vector(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy, color = NULL), center = FALSE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vector_smooth(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy), eval_points = eval_points, conf_level = 0.9) +
  ggtitle("Smoothed Vector Field with Ellipse Intervals")


# Example 3: Wedge with eval_points
ggplot(sample_points, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_vector(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy, color = NULL), center = FALSE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vector_smooth(aes(fx = fx, fy = fy), eval_points = eval_points, pi_type = "wedge") +
  ggtitle("Smoothed Vector Field with Wedge Intervals")
